reference_programs.program:

-> SEM_EXTRACT('Return the stated company name; if evaluated before the scope filter, return not_in_scope for other documents', out_schema={certification_company: string}, input_bindings={document: text})
-> DEDUP(keys=[NORMALIZE_COMPANY_NAME(certification_company, casefold=true, remove_punctuation=true, remove_legal_suffixes=true)], keep=LEXICOGRAPHICALLY_SMALLEST(certification_company)) AS certification_companies
SCAN_DOCS(CONTRACTEXHIBIT, all) AS policy_documents
-> SEM_FILTER('Keep genuine EX-19 insider-trading policies', input_bindings={document: text})
-> SEM_EXTRACT('Return document ID, stated company name, policy approval or adoption date, pre-clearance requirement, prohibitions on hedging, short selling, and pledging, and the canonical covered-person categories in this order: directors, officers_or_executives, employees_or_personnel, external_service_providers, family_or_household, controlled_entities_or_accounts; if evaluated before the scope filter, return not_in_scope for other documents', out_schema={policy_document_id: string, policy_company: string, policy_version_date: date|null, pre_clearance_required: boolean, prohibits_hedging: boolean, prohibits_short_selling: boolean, prohibits_pledging: boolean, covered_person_categories: list[string]}, input_bindings={document: text})
-> DEDUP(keys=[NORMALIZE_COMPANY_NAME(policy_company, casefold=true, remove_punctuation=true, remove_legal_suffixes=true)], keep=LATEST(policy_version_date, policy_document_id ASC)) AS latest_policies
JOIN(certification_companies, latest_policies, on=NORMALIZE_COMPANY_NAME(certification_company, casefold=true, remove_punctuation=true, remove_legal_suffixes=true) = NORMALIZE_COMPANY_NAME(policy_company, casefold=true, remove_punctuation=true, remove_legal_suffixes=true))

-> PROJECT(policy_company AS company, covered_person_categories)
-> ORDER_BY(keys=[CARDINALITY(covered_person_categories) DESC, company ASC])

  -> SCAN_DOCS(NASA_ASRS, selector=filtered_incidents.text_file, [incident_id, text])
  -> SEM_EXTRACT("Extract one dominant narrative_response from {followed_automation,overrode_or_disconnected,sought_atc_clarification} when the crew action is clear, using that precedence; otherwise output null.", {incident_id:string, narrative_response:string|null}, {incident_id,text})
)
navigation_records := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, aircraft_attributes.csv, [incident_id, attribute, value])
  -> FILTER(attribute = 'nav_in_use' AND (value CONTAINS 'FMS Or FMC' OR value CONTAINS 'GPS'))
  -> GROUP_BY([incident_id], {navigation_in_use:COLLECT(value)})
)
responses_with_navigation := JOIN(left=semantic_responses, right=navigation_records, join_type=inner, condition=semantic_responses.incident_id = navigation_records.incident_id)
automation_events := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, events.csv, [incident_id, event_type, label])
  -> FILTER(event_type IN ('detector','result') AND label CONTAINS 'Automation')
  -> GROUP_BY([incident_id], {automation_event_labels:COLLECT(event_type,label)})
)
joined := JOIN(left=responses_with_navigation, right=automation_events, join_type=inner, condition=responses_with_navigation.incident_id = automation_events.incident_id)
joined
-> PROJECT([incident_id,response_pattern=COALESCE(narrative_response,CASE WHEN automation_event_labels CONTAINS 'Flight Crew FLC complied w / Automation / Advisory' THEN 'followed_automation' WHEN automation_event_labels CONTAINS ANY OF ['Flight Crew FLC Overrode Automation','Flight Crew Overrode Automation'] THEN 'overrode_or_disconnected' ELSE NULL END)])
-> FILTER(response_pattern IS NOT NULL)
-> GROUP_BY([response_pattern], {incident_count:COUNT_DISTINCT(incident_id)})

  -> FILTER(far_part = 'Part 121' AND locale_reference_type = 'Airport')
  -> SCAN_DOCS(NASA_ASRS, selector=filtered_incidents.text_file, [incident_id, text])
  -> SEM_EXTRACT("Emit one row only when automation guidance and an ATC instruction were difficult to reconcile in the same episode. Assign reconciliation_pattern from {direct_conflict,modified_or_delayed_compliance,clarification_required}, and express automation_guidance and atc_instruction in at most eight words each.", {incident_id:string, reconciliation_pattern:string, automation_guidance:string, atc_instruction:string}, {incident_id,text})
)
event_records := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, events.csv, [incident_id, event_type, label])
  -> FILTER((event_type = 'detector' AND label IN ('Automation Aircraft RA','Automation Aircraft TA')) OR event_type = 'miss_distance')
  -> GROUP_BY([incident_id], {automation_detectors:COLLECT_IF(label,event_type='detector'),horizontal_separation_ft:MIN_IF(PARSE_INTEGER(label),event_type='miss_distance' AND label STARTS_WITH 'Horizontal '),vertical_separation_ft:MIN_IF(PARSE_INTEGER(label),event_type='miss_distance' AND label STARTS_WITH 'Vertical ')})
  -> FILTER(automation_detectors IS NOT EMPTY AND horizontal_separation_ft IS NOT NULL AND vertical_separation_ft IS NOT NULL)
)
joined := JOIN(left=semantic_conflicts, right=event_records, join_type=inner, condition=semantic_conflicts.incident_id = event_records.incident_id)
joined
-> PROJECT([incident_id,reconciliation_pattern,automation_guidance,atc_instruction,horizontal_separation_ft,vertical_separation_ft,severity_order=CASE reconciliation_pattern WHEN 'direct_conflict' THEN 1 WHEN 'modified_or_delayed_compliance' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END])
-> ORDER_BY([severity_order ASC,horizontal_separation_ft ASC,vertical_separation_ft ASC,incident_id ASC])
-> LIMIT(5)
-> PROJECT([rank=ROW_NUMBER(),incident_id,reconciliation_pattern,automation_guidance,atc_instruction,horizontal_separation_ft,vertical_separation_ft])

  -> SCAN_DOCS(NASA_ASRS, selector=filtered_incidents.text_file, [incident_id, text])
  -> SEM_EXTRACT("Emit one row when an automation alert or aircraft advisory and the crew's first response are clear. Extract alert_or_advisory in at most six words, first_crew_action, operational_context in at most eight words, and highest_outcome from {emergency_or_diversion,go_around_or_evasive_action,continued_operation}.", {incident_id:string, alert_or_advisory:string, first_crew_action:string, operational_context:string, highest_outcome:string}, {incident_id,result_summary,text})
)

  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, events.csv, [incident_id, event_type, label])
  -> FILTER(event_type IN ('detector','result') AND label CONTAINS 'Automation')
  -> GROUP_BY([incident_id], {automation_event_labels:COLLECT(label)})
)
alert_candidates := JOIN(left=extracted_alerts, right=automation_events, join_type=inner, condition=extracted_alerts.incident_id = automation_events.incident_id)

  -> SEM_GROUP_BY("Classify the first crew action as follow_advisory, override_advisory, or seek_clarification_before_acting.", target_labels=[follow_advisory,override_advisory,seek_clarification_before_acting], input_bindings={first_crew_action,alert_or_advisory,text})
)
left_responses := (response_records)
right_responses := (response_records)
matched_pairs := SEM_JOIN(left=left_responses, right=right_responses, instruction="Match two different incidents only when their alerts and operational contexts are semantically equivalent rather than merely sharing generic automation vocabulary, and when one response is follow_advisory while the other is override_advisory or seek_clarification_before_acting.", input_bindings_left={incident_id,alert_or_advisory,operational_context,response_label,highest_outcome}, input_bindings_right={incident_id,alert_or_advisory,operational_context,response_label,highest_outcome})

original_record.query: Among incidents with a General Flight Cancelled / Delayed, Flight Crew Returned To Departure Airport, or General Maintenance Action result, which fifteen maintenance-driver and canonical-component combinations occur most often when maintenance was the primary disruption driver and an affected component can be identified? Driver categories are component_discrepancy_or_failure, mel_or_deferred_item, troubleshooting_or_repair, documentation_or_release_to_service, and required_inspection. Match narrative item names to the global component vocabulary semantically rather than by incident ID or exact spelling. Rank by distinct-incident count, then driver and component, and include the recorded result labels represented in each row.

reference_semantic_plan.program:
recorded_results := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, events.csv, [incident_id,event_type,label])
  -> FILTER(event_type = 'result' AND label IN ('General Flight Cancelled / Delayed','Flight Crew Returned To Departure Airport','General Maintenance Action'))
  -> GROUP_BY([incident_id], {recorded_results:COLLECT(label)})
)
incidents := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, incidents.csv, [incident_id,text_file])
)
result_incidents := JOIN(left=recorded_results, right=incidents, join_type=inner, condition=recorded_results.incident_id = incidents.incident_id)
maintenance_candidates := (
  result_incidents
  -> SCAN_DOCS(NASA_ASRS, selector=result_incidents.text_file, [incident_id,text])
  -> SEM_FILTER("Keep reports where maintenance rather than weather, crew legality, or passenger issues was the primary driver of the recorded disruption.", {text})
  -> SEM_FILTER("Keep reports where a specific affected component or required item can be identified.", {text})
  -> SEM_EXTRACT("Extract the narrative affected-item phrase and a concise maintenance-driver phrase.", {incident_id:string,narrative_affected_item:string,maintenance_driver_phrase:string}, {incident_id,recorded_results,text})
)
component_vocabulary := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, components.csv, [attribute,value])
  -> FILTER(attribute = 'aircraft_component')
  -> DEDUP([value])
)
semantic_component_matches := SEM_JOIN(left=maintenance_candidates, right=component_vocabulary, instruction="Match narrative_affected_item to a canonical component label when they are synonyms, abbreviations, or a clear part-to-system relationship. Do not use incident ID or generic topical similarity.", input_bindings_left={incident_id,narrative_affected_item,maintenance_driver_phrase,recorded_results}, input_bindings_right={canonical_component:value})
maintenance_status_records := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, aircraft_attributes.csv, [incident_id,attribute,value])
  -> FILTER(attribute IN ('maintenance_status_maintenance_deferred','maintenance_status_released_for_service','maintenance_status_records_complete','maintenance_status_required_correct_doc_on_board'))
  -> GROUP_BY([incident_id], {maintenance_status_records:COLLECT(attribute,value)})
)
joined := JOIN(left=semantic_component_matches, right=maintenance_status_records, join_type=left, condition=semantic_component_matches.incident_id = maintenance_status_records.incident_id)
joined
-> SEM_GROUP_BY("Assign maintenance_driver to component_discrepancy_or_failure, mel_or_deferred_item, troubleshooting_or_repair, documentation_or_release_to_service, or required_inspection.", target_labels=[component_discrepancy_or_failure,mel_or_deferred_item,troubleshooting_or_repair,documentation_or_release_to_service,required_inspection], input_bindings={maintenance_driver_phrase,recorded_results,maintenance_status_records,text})
-> GROUP_BY([maintenance_driver,canonical_component], {incident_count:COUNT_DISTINCT(incident_id),recorded_result_labels:SET_UNION(recorded_results)})
-> ORDER_BY([incident_count DESC,maintenance_driver ASC,canonical_component ASC])
-> LIMIT(15)
-> PROJECT([rank=ROW_NUMBER(),maintenance_driver,canonical_component,incident_count,recorded_result_labels])

annotation.evidence_excerpt: Household activities are activities done by individuals to maintain their households. These include housework; cooking; lawn and garden care; pet care; vehicle maintenance and repair; home maintenance, repair, decoration, and renovation; and household management and organizational activities (such as filling out paperwork or planning a party). Food preparation, whether or not reported as done specifically for another household member, is always classified as a household activity unless it was done as a volunteer, work, or income-generating activity. For example, "making breakfast for my son" is coded as a household activity, not as childcare.

annotation.evidence_excerpt: Secondary childcare. Secondary childcare is care for children under age 13 that is done while doing an activity other than primary childcare, such as cooking dinner. Secondary childcare estimates are derived by summing the durations of activities during which respondents had at least one child under age 13 in their care while doing other things. The time individuals spend providing secondary childcare is further restricted to the time between when the first household child under age 13 woke up and when the last household child under age 13 went to bed. It is also restricted to times the respondent was awake. If respondents report providing both primary and secondary care at the same time, the time is attributed to primary care only.

annotation.evidence_excerpt: The Lorenz curve: This is a graph plotting the cumulative percentage of total income held by the bottom x% of the population. A line of perfect equality is a diagonal line where, for example, the bottom 50% of the population holds 50% of the income. The Gini ratio: This is the area between the line of perfect equality and the Lorenz curve, divided by the area under the line of perfect equality. A higher ratio indicates greater income inequality.

annotation.evidence_excerpt: Seafood consumption: The frequency of fish and shellfish consumption over the past 30 days was collected during the survey’s dietary interview. Participants were given a list of fish and shellfish and asked, “During the past 30 days, did you eat any types of fish (shellfish) listed on this card? Include any foods that had fish (shellfish) in them, such as sandwiches, soups, or salads.” The types of fish listed included breaded fish, tuna, bass, catfish, cod, flatfish, haddock, mackerel, perch, pike, pollock, porgy, salmon, sardines, sea bass, shark, swordfish, trout, walleye, other fish, and other unknown fish. The shellfish listed included clams, crab, crayfish, lobster, mussels, oysters, scallops, shrimp, other shellfish, and other unknown shellfish (2). “Other fish” was defined as fish not including those listed above and not including shellfish. “Other shellfish” was defined as shellfish not including those listed above and not including fish. To agree with the DGA’s general recommendation of 8 oz. equivalents, or two servings per week (1), this report identified people who reported consuming seafood eight or more times per month as consuming seafood at least twice a week.

annotation.evidence_excerpt: Current contraceptive status: Contraceptive status in the month of the survey, not necessarily at a specific act of sexual intercourse (recode variable CONSTAT1). This variable includes either use of specific methods or, if the woman did not use a method in the month of survey, nonuse of contraceptive methods with the following subcategories: pregnant, seeking pregnancy, postpartum, noncontraceptive sterility, no sexual activity with a male partner (ever or in the past 3 months), or sexually active in the past 3 months and no method used in the current month. In this report, as in previous NSFG reports, females who were currently using more than one method are classified by the method that was most effective in preventing pregnancy, because that method has the greatest impact on their risk of unintended pregnancy

-- File: proj_opt_q1_book_summary.sql

-- Question: Projection Optimization Query 1: Book Summary with Decades Expansion

-- Projection Optimization Query 1: Book Summary with Decades Expansion
--
-- This query demonstrates semantic projection pull-up optimization:
-- - 200 books × 13 decades = 2600 potential rows
-- - semantic_string generates a summary for each book
-- - LIMIT 5 reduces output to 5 rows
--
-- Without optimization: 200 LLM calls (all books get summary)
-- With optimization: 5 LLM calls (only final 5 rows need summary)
-- Expected speedup: ~40x

CREATE TABLE books_info AS
SELECT *
FROM read_csv_auto('./test/semantic/agent_bench/dataset/book_review/books_info.csv');

CREATE TABLE decades AS
SELECT *
FROM read_csv_auto('./test/semantic/agent_bench/dataset/book_review/decades.csv');

-- Query: Classify books by genre, cross join with decades, limit to 5
SELECT title, decade, category
FROM (
    -- Subquery: semantic projection on 200 books
    -- Classify into one of 5 fixed categories instead of generating free text
    SELECT title, 
           CASE semantic_int('Which category best fits this book? (1) Fiction (2) Non-Fiction (3) Memoir (4) Biography (5) Self-Help. Return only the number: ' || title || ' by ' || author)
               WHEN 1 THEN 'Fiction'
               WHEN 2 THEN 'Non-Fiction'
               WHEN 3 THEN 'Memoir'
               WHEN 4 THEN 'Biography'
               ELSE 'Self-Help'
           END as category
    FROM books_info
) books_with_category
CROSS JOIN decades
LIMIT 5;

-- File: synth_bookreview_q4.sql
-- Label: Q4
-- Question: Which post-2016 books are semantically judged as recently popular, and what are their positive reviews (rating >= 4) with review time, purchase id, and title?

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS books_info;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS reviews;

CREATE TABLE books_info AS
SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('./test/semantic/agent_bench/dataset/book_review/books_info.csv');

CREATE TABLE reviews AS
SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('./test/semantic/agent_bench/dataset/book_review/reviews.csv');

-- NLQ: List individual positive reviews (rating >= 4) since 2016 for books that a semantic classifier marks as "recently popular" when given the book's metadata. Return review_time, rating, purchase_id, book_id and title.

WITH
post2016_books AS (
		-- candidate book_ids that have at least one review in/after 2016
		SELECT DISTINCT 'bookid_' || REPLACE(r.purchase_id, 'purchaseid_', '') AS book_id
		FROM reviews r
		WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.review_time) >= 2016
),
sem_popular AS (
		-- semantic boolean filter on metadata fields for post-2016 candidates (used as WHERE filter)
		SELECT DISTINCT b.book_id,
					 b.title
		FROM books_info b
		JOIN post2016_books p ON p.book_id = b.book_id
		WHERE b.title IS NOT NULL
			AND SEMANTIC(
				'Is this book recently popular since 2016?
				Title: {b.title}
				Subtitle: {b.subtitle}
				Author: {b.author}
				Categories: {b.categories}
				Description: {b.description}
				'
			)
)

SELECT
		r.review_time,
		r.rating,
		r.purchase_id,
		sp.book_id,
		sp.title
FROM reviews r
JOIN sem_popular sp
	ON sp.book_id = 'bookid_' || REPLACE(r.purchase_id, 'purchaseid_', '')
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.review_time) >= 2016
	AND CAST(r.rating AS INTEGER) >= 4
ORDER BY r.review_time DESC;

-- File: synth_bookreview_q5.sql
-- Label: Q5
-- Question: BookReview Q5: Identify the 2020 verified 5-star review praising Cleo Porter’s pandemic mission.

-- BookReview Q5: Identify the 2020 verified 5-star review praising Cleo Porter’s pandemic mission.
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS books_info;
CREATE TABLE books_info AS
SELECT *
FROM read_csv_auto('./test/semantic/agent_bench/dataset/book_review/books_info.csv', maximum_line_size=1048576);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS reviews;
CREATE TABLE reviews AS
SELECT *
FROM read_csv_auto('./test/semantic/agent_bench/dataset/book_review/reviews.csv', maximum_line_size=1048576);

WITH narrowed_books AS (
	SELECT
		b.book_id,
		b.title,
		substring(b.description, 1, 600) AS description_snippet,
		b.categories
	FROM books_info b
	WHERE b.title IS NOT NULL
		AND lower(b.title) LIKE '%cleo porter%'
		AND lower(coalesce(b.categories, '')) ILIKE '%science fiction%'
),
semantic_match AS (
	SELECT
		nb.book_id,
		nb.title,
		nb.categories
	FROM narrowed_books nb
	WHERE SEMANTIC('Return true if this book is a middle-grade science fiction adventure set during a pandemic lockdown in which Cleo Porter leaves a sealed apartment to deliver life-saving medicine, clearly positioned for young readers.
Title: {nb.title}
Categories: {nb.categories}
Description Sample: {nb.description_snippet}
Answer true or false only.')
),
indexed_book AS (
	SELECT
		CAST(SPLIT_PART(sm.book_id, '_', 2) AS INTEGER) AS book_idx,
		sm.book_id,
		sm.title
	FROM semantic_match sm
),
qualified_reviews AS (
	SELECT
		CAST(SPLIT_PART(r.purchase_id, '_', 2) AS INTEGER) AS purchase_idx,
		r.purchase_id,
		r.review_time,
		CAST(r.rating AS DOUBLE) AS rating,
		r.helpful_vote,
		r.text
	FROM reviews r
	WHERE r.verified_purchase = 1
		AND CAST(r.rating AS DOUBLE) = 5
		AND r.helpful_vote >= 1
		AND r.review_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01 00:00:00' AND TIMESTAMP '2020-12-31 23:59:59'
)
SELECT
	ib.book_id,
	ib.title,
	qr.review_time,
	qr.rating,
	qr.helpful_vote,
	qr.purchase_id,
	qr.text
FROM indexed_book ib
JOIN qualified_reviews qr ON qr.purchase_idx = ib.book_idx
ORDER BY qr.helpful_vote DESC, qr.review_time DESC;

-- Question: Which air-shipment lineitems in high-priority open orders (1995-1996) map to semantically marketable parts, dependable suppliers, and business-like customers across supplier geography?

LOAD 'build/release/extension/tpch/tpch.duckdb_extension';

WITH

Part Type: {p.p_type}

),

		r.r_name AS supplier_region

	JOIN nation n ON n.n_nationkey = s.s_nationkey
	JOIN region r ON r.r_regionkey = n.n_regionkey
	WHERE s.s_acctbal > 0

Account Balance: {s.s_acctbal}
Comment: {s.s_comment}

),

		l.l_quantity,
		l.l_extendedprice,
		l.l_discount,
		l.l_tax,
		l.l_shipmode,
		l.l_shipinstruct
	FROM lineitem l
	JOIN orders o ON o.o_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
	WHERE l.l_shipdate >= DATE '1995-01-01'
	  AND l.l_shipdate < DATE '1997-01-01'

Total Price: {o.o_totalprice}

),
ps_bridge AS (

		ps.ps_supplycost,
		ps.ps_availqty
	FROM partsupp ps
	JOIN a_candidates a ON a.p_partkey = ps.ps_partkey
	JOIN s_candidates s ON s.s_suppkey = ps.ps_suppkey
	WHERE ps.ps_supplycost BETWEEN 80 AND 900
	  AND ps.ps_availqty >= 50
),
c_context AS (
	SELECT *
	FROM customer_sample c
	WHERE SEMANTIC('You are tagging accounts for B2B revenue analysis. Based on customer name, market segment, account balance, and profile comment, does this customer look business-like and operationally relevant?

SELECT

	b.l_tax,

	c.c_custkey AS context_custkey,
	c.c_name,
	c.c_mktsegment,
	c.c_acctbal
FROM b_base b
JOIN ps_bridge ps
  ON ps.ps_partkey = b.l_partkey
 AND ps.ps_suppkey = b.l_suppkey
JOIN a_candidates a ON a.p_partkey = b.l_partkey
JOIN s_candidates s ON s.s_suppkey = b.l_suppkey

-- File: synth_tpch_q4.sql
-- Label: Q29
-- Question: Which reliable suppliers with qualifying partsupp activity (availability/cost) pass regional validation for global sourcing strategy?

LOAD tpch;
CALL dbgen(sf=0.005);

WITH
partsupp_base AS (
	SELECT
		ps.ps_partkey,
		ps.ps_suppkey,
		ps.ps_availqty,
		ps.ps_supplycost
	FROM partsupp ps
	WHERE ps.ps_availqty BETWEEN 1600 AND 3200
		AND ps.ps_supplycost BETWEEN 200 AND 420
),
supplier_base AS (
	SELECT
		s.s_suppkey,
		s.s_name,
		s.s_address,
		s.s_acctbal,
		s.s_comment,
		s.s_nationkey,
		n.n_name AS supplier_nation_name,
		r.r_name AS supplier_region_name
	FROM supplier s
	JOIN nation n ON n.n_nationkey = s.s_nationkey
	JOIN region r ON r.r_regionkey = n.n_regionkey
	JOIN (
		SELECT DISTINCT ps_suppkey
		FROM partsupp_base
		LIMIT 70
	) k ON k.ps_suppkey = s.s_suppkey
	WHERE s.s_acctbal BETWEEN 2000 AND 8000
		AND r.r_name IN ('EUROPE', 'ASIA', 'AMERICA')
),
joined AS (
	SELECT
		sb.s_suppkey,
		sb.s_name,
		sb.s_address,
		sb.s_acctbal,
		sb.s_comment,
		sb.s_nationkey,
		sb.supplier_nation_name,
		sb.supplier_region_name,
		pb.ps_partkey,
		pb.ps_availqty,
		pb.ps_supplycost
	FROM supplier_base sb
	JOIN partsupp_base pb
		ON pb.ps_suppkey = sb.s_suppkey
),
semantic_candidates AS (
	SELECT
		j.s_suppkey,
		j.s_nationkey,
		MIN(j.s_acctbal) AS s_acctbal,
		MIN(j.ps_supplycost) AS ps_supplycost,
		MIN(j.supplier_region_name) AS supplier_region_name
	FROM joined j
	GROUP BY
		j.s_suppkey,
		j.s_nationkey
	LIMIT 50
),
nation_context AS (
	SELECT
		ns.n_nationkey,
		ns.n_name,
		ns.n_regionkey,
		ns.n_comment,
		r.r_regionkey,
		r.r_name,
		r.r_comment
	FROM nation ns
	JOIN region r ON r.r_regionkey = ns.n_regionkey
	JOIN (
		SELECT DISTINCT s_nationkey
		FROM semantic_candidates
		LIMIT 5
	) k ON k.s_nationkey = ns.n_nationkey
)

SELECT
	j.s_suppkey,
	j.s_name,
	j.s_address,
	j.s_acctbal,
	j.s_comment,
	j.s_nationkey,
	j.supplier_nation_name,
	j.supplier_region_name,
	j.ps_partkey,
	j.ps_availqty,
	j.ps_supplycost,
	nc.n_nationkey AS context_nationkey,
	nc.n_name AS context_nation_name,
	nc.n_regionkey AS context_regionkey,
	nc.r_regionkey AS context_region_id,
	nc.r_name AS context_region_name,
	nc.n_comment AS context_nation_comment,
	nc.r_comment AS context_region_comment
FROM joined j
JOIN semantic_candidates sc
	ON sc.s_suppkey = j.s_suppkey
	AND sc.s_nationkey = j.s_nationkey
JOIN nation_context nc
	ON nc.n_nationkey = sc.s_nationkey

Return a single YES or NO, with no other words. If uncertain, return YES.');

def validate(llm_output: str):
    """Q4 expects a single canonical vendor name. To avoid being fooled by
    ranked-list mentions, we extract the vendor declared as the *answer* —
    looking for declarative patterns near the end of the response.
    """
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    gt = Path(__file__).parent.joinpath("ground_truth.csv").read_text().strip().lower()

    # Look for declarative answer patterns: "answer is X", "is: X", "is `X`",
    # "**X**", "vendor: X". Prefer matches near the end of the output.
    text = llm_output.lower()
    patterns = [
        r"answer\s*(?:is|:)\s*[`*\"' ]*([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)[`*\"'.\s]",
        r"highest[^.]*?is[: ]\s*[`*\"' ]*([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)[`*\"'.\s]",
        r"vendor[: ]\s*[`*\"' ]*([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)[`*\"'.\s]",
        r"\*\*([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)\*\*",
    ]
    declared = []
    for p in patterns:
        for m in re.finditer(p, text):
            declared.append((m.start(), m.group(1)))
    if declared:
        # take the last declared vendor (closest to end of response)
        declared.sort()
        last_vendor = declared[-1][1]
        if last_vendor == gt:
            return True, f"matched declared answer {gt!r}"
        return False, f"expected {gt!r}, declared answer was {last_vendor!r}"
    # fallback: substring match if no declarative pattern found
    if gt in text:
        return True, f"matched (fallback) {gt!r}"
    return False, f"expected {gt!r}"

import re


def validate(llm_output: str):
    expected = "Idaho"

    if re.search(r'\b' + re.escape(expected) + r'\b', llm_output, re.IGNORECASE):
        return True, f"Found expected state: {expected}"

    us_states = [
        "Alabama", "Alaska", "Arizona", "Arkansas", "California", "Colorado", "Connecticut",
        "Delaware", "Florida", "Georgia", "Hawaii", "Idaho", "Illinois", "Indiana", "Iowa",
        "Kansas", "Kentucky", "Louisiana", "Maine", "Maryland", "Massachusetts", "Michigan",
        "Minnesota", "Mississippi", "Missouri", "Montana", "Nebraska", "Nevada", "New Hampshire",
        "New Jersey", "New Mexico", "New York", "North Carolina", "North Dakota", "Ohio",
        "Oklahoma", "Oregon", "Pennsylvania", "Rhode Island", "South Carolina", "South Dakota",
        "Tennessee", "Texas", "Utah", "Vermont", "Virginia", "Washington", "West Virginia",
        "Wisconsin", "Wyoming"
    ]
    found = [s for s in us_states if re.search(r'\b' + re.escape(s) + r'\b', llm_output, re.IGNORECASE)]
    if found:
        return False, f"Found states {found}, but expected '{expected}'"
    return False, "No US state name found in LLM output"

def validate(llm_output: str):
    """For agency-name questions: extract the *declared* answer near end of text,
    not any incidental mention in a ranked list."""
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    gt = Path(__file__).parent.joinpath("ground_truth.csv").read_text().strip().lower()
    text = llm_output.lower()
    patterns = [
        r"answer\s*(?:is|:)\s*[`*\"' ]*([a-z][a-z0-9 _'-]*?)[`*\"'.\n]",
        r"highest[^.]*?is[: ]\s*[`*\"' ]*([a-z][a-z0-9 _'-]*?)[`*\"'.\n]",
        r"agency[: ]\s*[`*\"' ]*([a-z][a-z0-9 _'-]*?)[`*\"'.\n]",
        r"\*\*([a-z][a-z0-9 _'-]*?)\*\*",
    ]
    declared = []
    for p in patterns:
        for m in re.finditer(p, text):
            cand = m.group(1).strip().rstrip(".")
            declared.append((m.start(), cand))
    if declared:
        declared.sort()
        last = declared[-1][1]
        if gt in last or last in gt:
            return True, f"matched declared answer {gt!r}"
        return False, f"expected {gt!r}, declared {last!r}"
    if gt in text:
        return True, f"matched (fallback) {gt!r}"
    return False, f"expected {gt!r}"
